  CITY OF SANTA MONICA

  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES

  MAY 12, 2026

  A special meeting of the Santa Monica City Council was called to order by Mayor Torosis at 5:35 p.m., on
  Tuesday, May 12, 2026, at City Council Chambers, 1685 Main Street, Santa Monica, CA.

  Roll Call:  Present:  Mayor Caroline Torosis
  Mayor Pro Tem Jesse Zwick
  Councilmember Lana Negrete
  Councilmember Dan Hall
  Councilmember Ellis Raskin
  Councilmember Barry Snell
  Councilmember Natalya Zernitskaya

  Also Present:  City Manager Oliver Chi
  City Attorney Heidi von Tongeln
  Interim City Clerk Denise Anderson-Warren

  CONVENE/PLEDGE  On order of the Mayor, the City Council convened at 5:35 p.m., with all
  members present. Councilmember Negrete led the assemblage in the Pledge
  of Allegiance.

  STATEMENT OF  The City of Santa Monica Statement of Accountability (Land
  ACCOUNTABILITY  Acknowledgement) was read into the record by Councilmember Hall.
  (LAND
  ACKNOWLEDGEMENT)

  LEVINE ACT  No Councilmembers made disclosures regarding the Levine Act (Govt Code
  DISCLOSURE  Section 84308).

  PUBLIC INPUT ON  Members of the public Brett Morrow, Karen Croner, Ashley Oelsen, Mitch
  REMAINING AGENDA  Silverstein, Eugenia Ermacora, Maddy Utrecht, Andrinka Payne, and Emma
  ITEMS:  Voigt commented on item 16.A.

  COUNCILMEMBER  In accordance with Council Rule 6(y), all Councilmember Discussion items
  DISCUSSION ITEMS:  were considered and approved in one motion unless removed by a
  Councilmember for discussion.

  1  May 12, 2026
 Docusign Envelope ID: 88E445D9-D048-884D-8278-F75F04E4C772

  16.A. Request of Mayor Torosis, Councilmember Raskin and
  Councilmember Snell to hold a special meeting to receive a briefing on
  significant progress in the City of Santa Monica's (City) long-standing
  pursuit of a certified Local Coastal Program (LCP), to memorialize the
  work underway, and to provide Council direction on how to carry this
  progress forward, was presented.

  Not knowing where the conversation on this item may go, Mayor Pro Tem
  Zwick recused himself from this item, out of an abundance of caution, due
  to his employment with the Housing Action Coalition, which advocates for
  Mayor Pro Tem Zwick was  housing production.
  excused at 11:20 p.m.
  Questions asked, included: what would the process look like on the back
  end, after the MOU; what is the relation of our local measure Proposition S
  from 1990, and how the beach overlay district relates to a potential LCP;
  what are the boundaries, are they 1000 yards from the coast; is the timeline
  to establish the MOU a year from now, and is that doable; how did this
  item come to become an emergency item, and what propelled it to become
  so urgent; is there a way to put up the historical facts update and where the
  city is on a website that follows along with the local coastal plan; is there a
  timeline and better understanding of the LCP, and why and when the
  timeline restarted; are there any state laws that have exempted certain types
  of projects from the Coastal Commission review already, and if that is the
  case, is there any way to provide some clarity on what webpage is being
  created about the LCP; which of the long standing policy disagreements are
  being talked about here; explain what is meant by ministerial CDP
  framework for certain categories of low impact projects; and, what are the
  project categories qualifying under ministerial CDP framework, what are
  the thresholds for those, and who determines that.

  Considerable discussion ensued, but limited to suggestions on what Council
  would like to see in an LCP; all things that are concurrently being worked
  on, with other efforts around the business renovations and things to make
  events and businesses easier; include all types of housing, starting with 100%
  deed restricted affordable housing in our coastal zone; adaptive reuse of
  buildings into housing; no new development, but the ability to convert vacant
  buildings into housing; maintain beach overlay district; support for the
  Coastal Plan, but not supportive of AB 1740; make sure to prioritize previous
  policy disagreements, including parking pricing, home sharing, preferential
  parking districts, and demolition; bus only and bike lanes need to be
  prioritized for streamlined approval; commercial changes in use are
  important for our economic recovery; we need to have some type of
  agreement with coastal on some of these major events that are forthcoming,
  and what that process looks like, and if that could be in an MOU; and, for
  commercial changes of use to also include potential renovations that would
  be required to facilitate changes to use, like outdoor bars and patios that
  businesses have proposed.

  2  May 12, 2026
 Docusign Envelope ID: 88E445D9-D048-884D-8278-F75F04E4C772

  Motion by Councilmember Hall, seconded by Councilmember Snell, to
  approve the recommendation, with direction to continue exploring policies
  consistent with our legislative platforms, and projects that we’ve been
  seeking approval recently. The motion was approved by the following vote:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Zernitskaya, Snell, Raskin, Hall, Negrete,
  Mayor Torosis
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Mayor Pro Tem Zwick

  ADJOURNMENT  On order of the Mayor, the City Council meeting adjourned at 12:14 a.m.
